stories.story_title: Nome-to-Kotzebue GeoAI prototype makes humans choose route trade-offs
stories.summary_2_sentences: A September 8 preprint tests an Arctic route-planning system on Nome–Kotzebue. It combines conversational AI, deterministic routing and separate human-selected equity judgments.
stories.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: The actual experiment concerns a Western Alaska supply corridor, with habitat and community exposure included in the decision.

sources.author: Samira Alkaee Taleghan; Younghyun Koo; Farnoush Banaei-Kashani

stories.confidence: high for what authors report; research validity not independently replicated
stories.status: Research prototype and author preprint; no verified operational vessel deployment
paper_facts: Colorado Denver/Colorado Boulder team; NSF grant 2531101.
Scenario: 6 m draft + 2 m margin; 12 knots; 3 km grid; 250 km corridor buffer.
May 20 and September 3, 2026 departures compare archived ice and forecast conditions.
At epsilon 0.35, reported searches completed in 371 and 715 seconds; spatial deduplication yielded nine and eight corridors.
No support for time-dependent multi-criteria routing.
User supplies criterion weights and equity assumptions; deterministic critic checks outputs.

exact_short_quote.text: Missing evidence is not treated as zero

repository_facts: The language model is optional; routing analysis does not use it and returns unchanged results without one.
Default local conversational model is llama3.1:8b through Ollama; rule-based fallback is supported.
Community indicators are not shipped. A separate public-data snapshot must be built before the equity lens works; otherwise it reports unavailable.
README explicitly identifies the tool as research decision support, unsuitable as navigational advice.
project_page_facts: Names Nome and Kotzebue; its 160 nautical-mile direct line is explicitly endpoint distance, not a navigable route.
Uses public sea-ice, bathymetry, weather, habitat and community/subsistence data.
Screenshot caption marks the community data tile unavailable, despite nearby static source cards showing full coverage; avoid claiming complete community coverage.

story_fuel.angle_inference: The most interesting design decision is where AI stops: it can ask what matters, while people choose the values and algorithms show consequences.
story_fuel.visual_opportunity: One supply boat splits into several map corridors; a human selector changes the preferred path, while unknown data remains a visible hole.
story_fuel.honest_tension: A mathematically consistent route comparison still depends on chosen values and incomplete evidence.
story_fuel.avoid: Do not call this an autonomous ship, real voyage, proven safety improvement, or local deployment. Do not conflate the language model with the routing algorithm.

local_sentiment.note: Targeted paper/author/Nome–Kotzebue searches found no independent Alaska community reaction. Public datasets do not demonstrate community consent or consultation.
